thesis: Costco has verified membership-driven compounding and strong liquidity, but the bear carries the purchase-price objection. At 45.40x tariff-normalized FY earnings and 2.26% annual FCF yield, the investor accepts a demanding return starting point despite strong operations. That is sufficient to defer aggressive entry, not proof that the enduring franchise should be sold.
strongest_counterexample: Annual FCF increased from $7.837bn to $9.390bn, operating margin improved to 3.85%, and membership fees rose to $5.907bn; continued compounding could justify the premium and outperform waiting.
invalidation_conditions: A subsequent fiscal year with operating margin above 3.85% and FCF growth above the observed approximately 19.8% would strengthen the compounding case enough to reopen the valuation-restraint ruling.
Annual FCF below $9.390bn and membership fees below $5.907bn would invalidate the current quality counterweight.
decisive_factors: Removing the small $0.15 tariff EPS benefit leaves the valuation demanding rather than destroying the growth case.
Working-capital contribution qualifies cash recurrence; cash and stated debt are already disclosed.
